title: Lafise Bank — Poket
overview: DISCOVER & IDEATION — USER TESTING RESEARCH · MVP DESIGN PLAN
overviewText: User Research for Digital Merchants — A study to understand the needs of small entrepreneurs and validate hypotheses about digital payment products across Central America.

sections.label: WHAT THE BUSINESS WANTED TO VALIDATE
sections.content:
01 — Digital Payment Hypotheses: Validate core assumptions about merchant payment behaviour — whether entrepreneurs prefer digital solutions over traditional POS terminals and why.

02 — User Language & Priorities: Understand the mental model and vocabulary of small business owners when interacting with financial apps. Surface unmet needs and latent desires.

03 — Competitive Bias: Identify expectations shaped by competitor apps (WhatsApp Pay, Yappy) to inform differentiated positioning.

sections.label: RESEARCH METHODOLOGY
sections.body:
Moderated usability testing with think-aloud protocol. Conducted remotely and in-person across Costa Rica and Panama. High-fidelity clickable Figma prototype covering 5 core flows: Onboarding, Transfer, Payment Request, Dashboard, Account Settings.

User Groups: Young Professionals (22–30) · Mid-Career (31–45) · University Students (18–22) · Senior Users (55+) · Unbanked Merchants.

Metrics captured: Task completion rate, time-on-task, error rate, SUS score, NPS, and qualitative insights via rainbow spreadsheet analysis.

sections.label: PROCESS
sections.content:
Discover → Stakeholder interviews · Competitive analysis · User shadowing · Market research

Define → Affinity mapping · User personas · Jobs-to-be-done · Problem framing

Ideate → Design sprints · Sketching · Wireframes · Flow mapping

Design → Hi-fi prototypes · Component library · User testing · Iteration cycles

sections.label: 5 CRITICAL FINDINGS FROM MVP USER TESTING

items.title: Navigation Confusion
items.body: Users couldn't locate key features without guidance. Tab labels were ambiguous — 85% of participants couldn't find 'Request Payment'.

items.title: Transfer Friction
items.body: 7-step transfer flow created cognitive overload. 70% expected fewer taps. Fee disclosure only appeared at step 6 of 7.

items.title: Auth Overload
items.body: Biometric + PIN + OTP in the same session felt excessive. Senior users (55+) gave up on authentication in 40% of cases.

items.title: Error Handling
items.body: Generic errors ('Something went wrong') caused anxiety. 55% abandoned after first error screen with no recovery path.

items.title: Dashboard Clarity
items.body: Balance visibility praised by 80% of users. Transaction history was the strongest-performing section — clear and familiar.

sections.label: DESIGN DECISIONS
sections.content:
01 — Tab Bar Redesign: Moved Rewards to a dedicated tab. Added persistent text labels below all icons. Renamed 'Cobrar' → 'Recibir Pago' for clarity.

02 — SSO Integration: Enabled single sign-on across LAFISE banking products to reduce friction at login and eliminate duplicate auth steps.

03 — Smart Auth Tiers: Biometric-only for transfers under $50. PIN + biometric for $50–$500. Full OTP above $500. Risk-proportional security.

04 — Transfer Flow 7→4 Steps: Consolidated recipient + amount + fee disclosure into a single smart screen. Confirmation simplified to one tap.

05 — Contextual Error System: Replaced generic errors with specific messages + recovery paths. Each error type mapped to a tailored CTA.

06 — Membership Tiers + Rewards: Tiered UI with clear perks per level. Gamification mechanics ('earn & spend') added to transaction confirmations.

sections.label: REFLECTION
sections.content: Designing Poket taught me that financial inclusion isn't just about features — it's about trust. Every extra authentication step, every ambiguous label, every generic error message erodes confidence in a product that holds people's money. The SUS score of 62.5 was a clear signal, not a failure — it was the data we needed to redesign with purpose. Seeing merchants across Costa Rica and Panama use a simpler, faster product is what the work was really about.
